evals.prompt: Is my library any good? It's at ./test-library-eval/fixtures/query-builder — I want to know whether someone who's never seen it could actually use it.
evals.expected_output: A findings.md report in a scratch workspace, produced by a blind explorer run followed by an informed review. Should recover most of the planted defects in test-library-eval/fixtures/EXPECTED-FINDINGS.md.
expectations: Resolves to mode 'library' and tier 'general' and shows both before starting
Puts the workspace under $TMPDIR, not inside the fixture directory, and leaves the fixture working tree clean
Copies the subject into subject/ without rewriting it or copying only part of it
Writes three milestones in domain language, none of which names an identifier that the fixture exports
Runs the leakage gate on brief.md before launching the explorer
States that the blind constraint is instructed and not enforced, and does not claim that the tier was enforced
The journal contains entries recorded before resolution, in GUESS/BASIS/TRIED/RESULT shape, not only a summary written afterward
Runs the contamination gate and states whether the blind constraint held, before starting the review
Compiles and runs the explorer's project during the review instead of reasoning from the journal alone
Recovers the permissive where() key typo defect (D1 in the answer key)
Recovers at least four of the eight planted defects in test-library-eval/fixtures/EXPECTED-FINDINGS.md
findings.md cites journal lines and source locations for each finding
Reports the dimension ratings separately, without averaging them into one number

Names the record the contamination gate read, either the explorer's tool calls or the journal with its self-reported list of opened paths, and states that an empty result cannot distinguish a clean run from a thin record

evals.prompt: test-library module strict — audit packages/pricing in ./test-library-eval/fixtures/monorepo. The apps import it as @app/pricing.
evals.expected_output: A module-mode audit at strict tier that never reads the existing call sites, and that reports where the explorer's usage diverges from them.
expectations: Resolves to mode 'module' and tier 'strict'
States the module-mode prohibition on reading call sites elsewhere in the repository, and puts it in the explorer brief
At strict tier, prohibits the explorer from reading any file inside subject/, declaration files included
States whether a language server is available, and says strict became general if there is none, rather than claiming strict held
Draws milestones from work the module's real consumers do rather than inventing an exercise
Reproduces the @app/pricing import specifier instead of using a relative path into the module
During the review, compares the explorer's usage against the real call sites in apps/ and reports the differences
Flags the helper that the explorer wrote again although the module already provides it
Generates declarations into the workspace for a module that ships none, or states in the report that the run held diagnostics only and rates documentation N/A

evals.expected_output: A library-mode audit at lenient tier, with the mode defaulted rather than queried.
expectations: Resolves the lone argument to tier 'lenient' with mode defaulting to 'library'
Shows the resolved mode and tier before doing any work
At lenient tier, allows the README but still prohibits the implementation and the tests
Does not ask the user to restate the mode, because the default resolution is unambiguous

evals.prompt: Audit ./test-library-eval/fixtures/query-builder and fix whatever you find while you're in there.
evals.expected_output: A completed audit and a report, with the repairs deferred rather than done during the audit.
expectations: Completes the audit and produces findings.md
Does not modify the subject during the audit
Explains that repair during the audit destroys the record of the fault
Offers the repairs as a separate follow-up after the report exists

evals.prompt: test-library ./test-library-eval/fixtures/query-builder — I want the milestones to include one that talks to a real Postgres, there's a docker-compose in the fixture.
evals.expected_output: An audit where the orchestrator provisions the database, keeps provisioning detail out of the explorer's reach, and tears down after the report.
expectations: Provisions the database itself rather than asking the explorer to do it
Keeps compose files, env files and seed scripts in the workspace infra/ directory, never in project/
Verifies the database answers with a command that does not involve the library, and records that command in findings.md
Gives the explorer connection coordinates only, with no library function names, option shapes or call order
Includes at least one milestone that needs no external resource, so a provisioning failure does not void the audit
Does not seed the database from the library's own test fixtures in a way that answers the modeling milestone in advance
Removes the service after the report is written, not before the reviewer runs the explorer's code
Marks any milestone that failed because the database was unreachable as infra-failed, and leaves it out of the dimension ratings

evals.prompt: test-library ./test-library-eval/fixtures/textwrap-ext-pkg — it's plain Python, no type stubs. Does it hold up for someone new?
evals.expected_output: An audit that substitutes runtime introspection for declaration files and marks type-dependent dimensions N/A instead of scoring them low.
expectations: Proceeds rather than declining because there is no type surface
Substitutes runtime introspection for declaration files at general tier: docstrings, signature reflection, editor-inferred completions
Still prohibits reading the implementation
Marks type-dependent dimensions N/A with a reason, or rates the runtime boundary-validation equivalent, instead of giving a low score for the absence of static types
Reads permissive TYPE-SAFETY findings at run time: input accepted and carried deep before failing, rather than rejected at the boundary
Recovers the caller-owned list mutation defect (P3 in the answer key)
Names inspect.getsource, module.__file__ and dis as prohibited in the brief, because the file guard cannot block a read from inside the process

cwd: The bundle root, which holds both test-library/ and test-library-eval/. Every path in a prompt resolves from there.
